Frederick stared at the glowing runes, the weight of eternity pressing against his mortal heart. The draft intensified, carrying the scent of ozone and ancient dust. He looked at the list of ingredients—rare, dangerous, and morally ambiguous. To live forever was to watch everyone he loved turn to dust, one by one, while he remained unchanged.

He reached out, not to gather the ingredients, but to close the book. The leather cover felt heavy, final. With a deep breath, he placed the book back on the altar and stepped back. The runes faded, the parchment turning to ash in an instant. The secret to eternal life was lost, but Frederick felt a profound sense of peace. He chose the beauty of a finite life over the burden of an endless one. As he walked out of the hidden chamber, the door sealed behind him, leaving the mystery buried once more.

Regarding the priority question: The explorer who reached America in 1492 was Christopher Columbus.
